chapter: On the road and later jobs
title: Two banjos, Jimmy Duport's place and Harold Christophe's call
summary: He recalls a band with two banjos including Willie, playing parties at Jimmy Duport's place, and his last job with Harold Christophe; his hands hurt.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: The final piece was most extreme. Second real of the band.

Then I had, I called it a banjo. One of the last I could get a guitar player, I called it a banjo player. Willie. Willie Van Teese. Oh yeah. Got him two banjos. Two banjos in your band. Yeah, two banjos. Sound good too. Willie had a good, real good banjo. Cause we was playing down on France Street. A fellow by the name of Jimmy Duport. But he couldn't get nobody in the place. Honestly they had a lot of sisters hanging that place, you know? Oh I see. And when he hired the band, he wanted a Dixieland band. Cause he knew me. He wanted me to play for different parties. Man, we were playing for parties around y'all like nobody's business. He even called me Fanny, he said Foot Warmers. That's what they announced me at a keynote game. I saw a holler there. I said, man that's Foot Warmers. I said, what was the name of the band? I said, I got some chords in there. I don't know where they are. I ain't played since last year. The last job we, I played in Tibidon not so long ago. Harold Christoff called me up and told me to say, He said, man you want to play a little job? I said, yeah man. He said, where you going? Even though he didn't tell me where he was going. He said, I'm going to pick you up by 12 o'clock. I said, okay. So he picked me up at 12 o'clock and said,
we're going to go to the table. We're going to the Donalstonville.
I said, why don't you tell me he was going to Donalstonville. I wouldn't play with you Jackie. You don't like Donalstonville?

No, I mean, I was feeling sick. You know what I mean? I was kind of sick. My hand was hurting me. My fingers been hurting me about a year, man. You know, what's wrong with it? Bad. Well, I played the piano, but it wasn't so bad playing the piano. You know, the band on it, you know. The banjo, kind of hurt sliding over the frecks, you know. Oh, yeah.
